title: Remote nonreciprocal magnon magnon entanglement via the Barnett effect with coherent feedback
authors: Jinhao Jia, Yingyu Li, Ran Liang, Qinghua Cai, Xin Wen, Mei Zhang
abstract: We propose a scheme for generating and controlling remote nonreciprocal magnon--magnon entanglement in a cavity magnonic system with coherent feedback.The two microwave cavities are driven by independent single-mode squeezed vacuum fields, with a rotating YIG sphere in the left cavity and a stationary one in the right cavity. For a fixed rotation direction, reversing the bias magnetic field applied to the rotating sphere changes the sign of the Barnett shift, leading to nonreciprocal magnon--magnon entanglement. By tuning the cavity detuning and feedback phase, entanglement can be generated for one direction of the bias magnetic field while it vanishes for the opposite direction, yielding complete nonreciprocity. Coherent feedback enhances the entanglement at an appropriate reflectivity, whereas stronger feedback can reduce it. The relative squeezing phase provides additional control, and an appropriate choice of unequal squeezing factors improves the entanglement at fixed total input photon occupation. With the squeezed inputs kept fixed, moderate feedback also increases the critical temperature for magnon entanglement.Our results provide a controllable approach to preparing remote nonreciprocal quantum correlations in cavity magnonic systems.
summary: This theoretical study proposes a controllable method to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement between magnons in a coupled cavity system. By leveraging the Barnett effect and implementing coherent quantum feedback, the authors show that the entanglement can be selectively generated for one direction of the applied magnetic field while suppressing it in the opposite direction. This offers a versatile platform for quantum information processing using magnonic circuits.
main_problem: The paper addresses the generation and control of remote nonreciprocal magnon-magnon entanglement in a coupled cavity magnonic system.
main_result: They demonstrate that nonreciprocal entanglement can be achieved by tuning the system parameters, specifically showing that entanglement exists for one direction of the bias magnetic field while vanishing for the opposite.
method: The analysis uses Quantum Langevin Equations (QLEs) to model the system dynamics and quantifies entanglement using the logarithmic negativity of the magnon covariance matrix.
model_or_system: The system consists of two microwave cavities coupled to YIG spheres (one rotating, one stationary) and driven by squeezed vacuum fields, incorporating the Barnett effect and a coherent feedback loop.
key_observables: Magnon-magnon entanglement ($E_N$), Asymmetry Contrast ($\xi_E$), and critical temperatures for entanglement vanishing.
important_parameters: Cavity detuning, feedback phase, relative squeezing phase, squeezing factors ($R_1, R_2$), and the sign of the Barnett shift ($\Delta B$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a lossless feedback loop and neglects propagation delay.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of entanglement ($E_N$) on the relative squeezing phase, feedback reflectivity ($r_b$), squeezing factors ($R_1$), and temperature ($T$) for both positive and negative Barnett shifts.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical model using QLEs, derives the necessary steady-state covariance matrix equations, and then systematically analyzes the entanglement measure ($E_N$) as a function of control parameters to establish the nonreciprocal control scheme.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics as it combines several advanced topics: cavity quantum electrodynamics (magnonics), non-Hermitian physics (via feedback), and the study of quantum correlations (entanglement) in solid-state systems.

Spintronics.note: The paper directly addresses magnon dynamics in coupled cavity systems (magnons coupled to cavities) and uses quantum-optical techniques (squeezed vacuum fields, entanglement quantification) within a magnetic system, fitting the core theme of magnon/photon polaritons and cavity QED in magnets.
